After months of Liquid Glass testing, WhatsApp is now expanding the scope of its new interface testing to the iPad app, adopting a Mac-like sidebar design. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing a brand new iPad app layout

WhatsApp began adapting its iOS app for the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul as early as last October, but it was not until this June that the new design was brought to the iPad in a limited beta test.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the new design featured Liquid Glass-styled tabs, buttons, and action menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

According to the latest report from the website, WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the existing bottom tab bar with a new Mac-like sidebar as the default interface.

This sidebar mimics the layout of WhatsApp for Mac, allowing users to quickly switch between sections such as "Chats", "Status", "Communities", "Calls", Meta AI, and other features. Users can also hide the sidebar to free up more space for the conversation list and chat window.

Here is the report content:

WABetaInfo mentioned that some beta testers running the latest TestFlight version have already been able to use the new sidebar, while some users on the regular App Store version are also beginning to see this new interface.

As is WhatsApp's usual practice, the new interface will take some time to roll out to all users, whether they are on the beta version or the official version. However, iPad users will ultimately benefit from this layout that is better suited for tablet use.
